`git merge` creates a merge commit that preserves the full history of both branches.

```bash
git merge feature
# Creates: [A---B---C---M] (M = merge commit)
```

`git rebase` rewrites history by replaying commits on top of the target branch.

```bash
git rebase main
# Creates: [A---B---C---D] (D = feature commits moved)
```

Use `merge` to preserve history and allow collaboration. Use `rebase` for clean, linear history on local branches only (never on shared branches).
